message.content:
My best guess is that a typical employee would urgently flag the conflict to the manager and, if there were no way to get approval before the cutoff, would probably extend this one box anyway and document why. The booked collection and the risk of destroying the only copies of the family letters and photos make the loss unusually concrete and irreversible, while the rework cost is relatively small.

That would be a prediction about likely human behavior, not a policy-compliant action: the pending request is not permission, and an unapproved date change would violate the policy and the manager’s instruction. A more risk-averse employee might instead release the batch as directed.
